reason: The two are almost identical, and both share the same flaws. The sage circle has moved in from its corner, so the SOLSTICE wordmark and the can now sit on top of it. The peach circle rises into the subhead line, and that collision makes the copy look crowded. A spreads the headline, subhead and CTA more evenly down the canvas. B packs that block higher, which leaves a larger empty area under the CTA.

Both make the same structural mistake. The headline 'Garden-fresh fizz' sits above the SOLSTICE wordmark, which reverses the brand-first reading order, and it runs into the sage circle at top right. Both also leave a large dead gap between the body copy and a shrunken can. A spreads its elements more evenly down the tall canvas, though its CTA crowds the peach circle at the bottom. B packs everything higher and leaves empty space below the CTA, and its can is slightly smaller, which makes the product feel less important.

The two layouts are nearly identical and share the same flaws. The VOLTSTRIDE box, which is the hero product, has shrunk to a tiny chip squeezed into the left gutter, and the 48H badge sits in that same narrow strip. The lime panel is pushed off-centre to the right, the headline runs almost to the panel's right edge, and a large empty gap separates the headline from the body copy and CTA. A is slightly better because its panel sits more evenly on the canvas. B's panel starts lower and ends only about 48px from the bottom edge, which crowds the bottom and leaves too much empty space at the top.

A: the logo is shrunk to an illegible scrap jammed into the card's top-left corner. The book cover, the key image, is reduced to a trivial thumbnail that straddles the card's bottom edge. The body copy is almost as big as the headline, and the CTA is cramped next to the fine print. B drops the book art entirely and its logo is also too small to read, but the hierarchy is clean (eyebrow, headline, copy, a clear CTA with legal text beneath). Its margins are more even, though there is dead space at the bottom of the card.

The two are almost the same. In both, the green circle has moved behind the SOLSTICE wordmark and the can, so the wordmark no longer sits on clean space as it did in the original. The peach circle also runs behind the start of the subhead and the left side of the CTA. A crowds the headline, subhead and CTA into a tight group and leaves about 140px of empty space below the CTA, so it looks top-heavy. B spreads the headline, subhead and CTA out more evenly down the canvas, which balances the layout slightly better, though its bottom area is still fairly empty.

Both put the headline above the SOLSTICE wordmark, which breaks the original's brand-first reading order, and the headline sits on top of the green circle. Both also shrink the can and leave dead space around it. A groups the headline, brand and body copy more tightly and leaves the CTA a little more room above the peach circle. In B the copy is spread more loosely, with a large empty gap between the can and the CTA, and the button crowds the peach circle.

The two layouts are almost the same and share the same faults. The lime panel is pushed against the right edge with an arbitrary gap on the left. There is a large dead area inside the panel between the headline and the body copy. The VOLTSTRIDE box, which is the hero product, has shrunk to a tiny fragment stuck to the left edge. The 48H ONLY badge is small and floats on its own. A's panel sits lower and leaves a thin bottom margin. B's panel sits higher and leaves a large stretch of empty stripes at the bottom. Neither difference is better or worse overall.

A: the layout is clean and readable, with a clear headline → copy → CTA order. But the book cover, the original's key image, is dropped entirely, and the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an illegible speck in the corner. B: the logo is tiny and clipped at the card edge, and the book cover is a thumbnail-sized leftover stranded below the card. The body copy is oversized and competes with the headline, while the CTA is shrunk and pushed beside equally small fine print. The card also nearly touches the right edge of the canvas.

Both keep the original's centred stack, but they move the decorative circles inward. The teal circle no longer bleeds off the edge: the 'GLACIER' wordmark sits on its edge and the can sits half over it. The legal line overlaps the light-blue circle and is tiny at this size. A also pushes the whole stack up, so legal ends around y=665 and leaves a dead band at the bottom while the top half feels crowded. B spaces the logo, can, headline, CTA and legal more evenly down the canvas and keeps the legal near the bottom margin, as in the original.

Both candidates have the same layout. In both, the three flavour chips are scattered on different rows and at different x-positions: Blood Orange sits low on the left, while Cucumber Mint and Honey Rosemary are stacked on the right. None of them line up with the text's left edge at x≈75. The Shop Flavours CTA floats off-axis to the right, and the bottom ~20% of the canvas is dead space apart from a cropped peach circle. B only moves the CTA and chip group down a few pixels, which gives the subhead slightly more room but fixes none of the alignment or grouping problems.

The two layouts are nearly identical, so I picked A only by a hair. Both have the same flaws: the flavour chips are scattered in a staggered layout off the grid (Blood Orange is offset from the two right-hand chips), the Shop Flavours button is off-centre and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge, the legal line is tiny, and the bottom third is mostly empty apart from a cropped circle. B moves the button, chips and legal text up, which jams the button against the subhead and leaves even more empty space at the bottom. A keeps slightly better spacing between those elements.

A packs everything into the top 60%, leaving roughly 300px of empty orange at the bottom. Its bottle cap almost touches the top edge, and the faint decorative circle overlaps the bottle's circle clumsily. B centres the stack vertically and keeps the decorative circle apart in the corner, so it is better balanced. Both share the same flaws: the headline is left-aligned while the NEW pill and Try It button are right-aligned, so there is no common axis, and the NEW badge floats away from the product it labels.

Both are essentially the square layout scaled down and centred on a taller canvas. In both, the pill tags and the URL line are now tiny, the 'missing asset' placeholder box is still there, and the can floats on its own to the right of the date block. A spreads the stack down the taller canvas so the top and bottom margins are more even. B compresses the content upward, which leaves a cramped middle and a large empty band at the bottom under the RSVP/URL group.

The two are almost identical: both enlarge the backdrop circle and pull it in from the edge, so it reads as a large blob crowding the lower right. Both leave a big empty band above the quote mark while the bottom half is crowded. A's attribution sits tight under the quote and its can floats high, away from the bottom edge where the original anchored it. B keeps the original's gap under the quote and sits the can lower, so it is slightly more faithful, but its logo still floats with no clear alignment to the can.

The two are almost the same. Both put the quote over a mostly empty top band about 140px tall. In both, the left circle sits fully inside the canvas instead of bleeding off the edge as in the original, and it now crowds the headline. Both leave a dead lower-left area where only the small SOLSTICE logo floats, and the can sits closer to the centre of the maroon circle than in the original, losing the original's bleed-off-the-corner tension. A squeezes the attribution up close under the headline, about 38px versus about 50px in the original. B keeps the original's gap between headline and attribution, so it is very slightly more faithful.

Both are near-identical rescales. The teal circle is pulled fully into the frame and sits behind the logo and the can, which muddies the GLACIER wordmark. The legal line sits on the light-blue circle, and the grey fine print is very small and low-contrast. A keeps the legal line near the bottom edge like the original and leaves more room above the headline. B lifts the headline/CTA cluster up, leaving a dead band of empty space at the bottom with the fine print floating in the middle of the circle, so B's vertical balance is slightly worse.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both have the same flaws. The CTA is centred off the left text edge, and the three flavour pills are scattered unevenly: Blood Orange sits alone on the left, and the other two are stacked to the right with mismatched widths. The pills read as random fragments rather than one group, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty except for the clipped peach circle. B squeezes the subtitle and CTA slightly closer to the headline, which makes the copy cluster a bit more cramped, so A has marginally better breathing room.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same flaws. The pills are scattered in a staggered arrangement, with Blood Orange dropped below Cucumber Mint, so they no longer read as one row. The Shop Flavours CTA floats off-centre to the right and lines up with neither the left-aligned headline nor the pills. The fine print is too small to read and is centred on a different axis from the copy. The empty bottom-left corner and the stray circle leave the balance lopsided. B wins only marginally: it adds a little more space between the subhead and the CTA and sits slightly lower, so A's cramped subhead-to-CTA gap and larger dead area at the bottom are a bit worse.

A sits roughly centred down the canvas, but the bottle medallion is small for a story format. A pale decorative circle floats alone in the top-left corner, and the right-aligned NEW and Try It pills don't line up with the left-aligned headline and bottle, so the layout looks split down the middle. B crams everything into the top 60% and leaves about 300px of dead orange at the bottom. Its bottle cap almost touches the top edge, and the decorative circle crowds the medallion, plus it has the same ragged left/right alignment.

Both are close to a uniform shrink of the original square, not a real rearrangement: the moon disc is cropped in the same way, the can floats loosely beside the details block, the pill badges and the URL line are tiny, and the 'missing asset' partner placeholder still sits orphaned at bottom right. A pushes the whole stack up and leaves about 140px of dead space at the bottom. B spreads the content over the taller canvas a little more evenly, with more room between the headline, the details and the CTA and a smaller empty band at the bottom, so it balances slightly better.

The two layouts are almost the same. In both, the beige circle has moved inward and floats as a large cropped disc, where in the original it was a corner bleed. Both also leave a dead band above the quote mark, and the logo row sits detached in the lower left. A has a slight edge because its quote, attribution, logo and can are spread more evenly down the page; B pushes them all upward, which leaves more empty space below the can and the logo.

A and B are nearly identical, and both make the same mistakes. The left circle no longer bleeds off the canvas edge as it does in the original. It now sits as a whole circle behind the quote and attribution, so it competes with the text. The product can stays small and floats inside the large maroon circle, and there is a lot of empty space below the attribution. A spaces the attribution slightly more like the original. B sits the sun closer to the can and moves the logo and can up a little. Neither difference makes one better than the other.
